stops.name: Fractured Crater-Floor Outcrop
stops.atLocation: Light-toned, polygonally fractured bedrock outcrop emerging along the eastern margin of the dark mafic crater-floor plain, surrounded by blocky regolith and small impact craters. Provides a stable, low-slope (5.0°) vantage point for inspecting exposed crater-floor stratigraphy.

reference.description: An eroded sedimentary remnant mound rising from the crater floor ahead of the main western delta escarpment, surrounded by wind-rippled sand bedforms. It exposes inclined foreset bedding layers deposited where an ancient river entered Lake Jezero, allowing astronauts to inspect deltaic stratigraphy from a safe standoff distance without climbing steep cliff slopes.
reference.whyItMatters: Preserves cross-sectional deltaic stratigraphy that records ancient lake-level fluctuations and fluvial sediment transport into Jezero Crater.

stops.name: Crater-Floor Scarp & Rim Bench
stops.atLocation: Positioned on the rocky southern rim of a prominent NW–SE crater-floor scarp overlooking a dune-filled trough to the northeast. The scarp wall exposes bright-toned fractured rock layers while keeping astronauts safely above the loose sand bedforms below.

reference.description: Fine-grained, polygonally fractured sedimentary bedrock on the lower delta apron where oxidized surface dust has been abraded away to expose fresh interior rock texture. This unit represents water-altered mudstone and sandstone beds mapped across the delta front with orbital aqueous mineral signatures.
reference.whyItMatters: Clay and carbonate minerals formed through past water–rock interaction are prime indicators of ancient habitable environments and past liquid water activity.

stops.name: Mafic Plateau Rim Bench
stops.atLocation: A flat, consolidated dark mafic rock bench along the western scarp edge, positioned safely south of the adjacent aeolian sand dune field and bordering bright fractured bedrock exposures. Offers firm, low-slope footing for close-up rock inspection and sample-preparation simulations.

reference.description: A flat, competent sedimentary bench along the western delta front exhibiting a circular surface abrasion patch cleared through the weathered outer rind. This surface preparation workflow allows close-up mineralogical inspection prior to subsurface sample extraction.
reference.whyItMatters: Removing the radiation-oxidized surface rind exposes pristine interior mineralogy needed to evaluate organic preservation potential and prioritize subsurface biosignature sampling.
